Looking at this question about the Nature 2016 paper on host regulators of metastatic colonization, I need to identify what protein TRAF1 associates with.

TRAF1 (TNF Receptor-Associated Factor 1) is a signaling adaptor protein. In the context of this paper, which identified host factors regulating metastatic colonization through genome-wide screening, TRAF1 was identified as one of the key regulators.

TRAF1 is well-known to directly associate with cIAP2 (cellular Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein 2). They form a stable heterodimer complex that plays a critical role in NF-κB signaling and inflammatory responses. This TRAF1-cIAP2 interaction is a direct protein-protein association, as opposed to NF-κB which is a downstream transcription factor in the signaling cascade.

[ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
